walkthroughs.title: Knee pain after twisting

doorway: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

timeline.student: We will protect the knee, assess stability and decide whether imaging is needed. I want to review it in one week. If it becomes hot and very swollen, you develop fever, or it locks, seek urgent assessment.
timeline.patient: Thank you. I understand that the next steps depend on the examination and tests.
timeline.why: Proposed care, not a record of tests or treatment already completed.

timeline.student: What questions do you have about the next steps?
timeline.patient: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.

timeline.student: We can document temporary lifting and squatting limits and discuss how you will manage stairs at home.
timeline.patient: That would help. Thank you.
timeline.why: Answer the concern that was just expressed. Give a defensible recommendation and explain uncertainty; do not promise a diagnosis or recovery before the evidence supports it.

note.S:
CC: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

HPI: 54-year-old male. Right knee pain for 3 days. Twisting injury on a planted foot while carrying a box; no fall. Medial right knee pain. No radiation. Aching with catching pain during rotation. Weight bearing with limp; pain 6/10. Delayed swelling over the first evening. Catching without true locking or giving way. Worse with twisting, stairs and deep flexion. Relief with rest, protected ice and elevation. Acetaminophen 650 mg twice yesterday. Prior activity-related ache and brief morning stiffness.

PMH: Hypertension; crystal-confirmed gout episode last year.

PSH: Hernia repair at 30; no knee surgery.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; no urate-lowering therapy.

SH: Former smoker: 5 pack-years, quit 15 years ago. Approximately six beers weekly. No recreational drugs. Grocery stocker; frequent lifting and squatting. Lives with wife; one flight of home stairs.

FH: Mother: knee osteoarthritis requiring replacement. Father: hypertension; brother: gout.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Musculoskeletal: Right knee swelling. No other current joint pain. No generalized myalgia. General: No fever. No chills. No systemic malaise. Neurologic: No distal numbness. No paresthesias. No distal weakness.
note.O:
Vitals: BP 138/84 mmHg, P 78 bpm, R 16 rpm, T 98.5 F oral, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 11", Wt 206 lbs

General: Alert, comfortable at rest.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Musculoskeletal: Small right knee effusion without erythema or deformity.
Musculoskeletal: Medial joint-line tenderness and mild warmth; no patellar or fibular-head tenderness.
Musculoskeletal: Right knee extends to 0 degrees and flexes to 110 degrees with pain near end flexion; mild crepitus.
Musculoskeletal: Knee extension 4+/5 limited by pain; ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion 5/5.
Musculoskeletal: Antalgic gait; able to take four steps.
Heart: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+ bilaterally.
Osteopathic: L4 right lumbar paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 2. Knee osteoarthritis with an acute flare
P: 1. Protect weight bearing as needed, avoid twisting/squatting and use ice, compression and elevation with safe analgesia. Assess fracture-imaging criteria and ligament stability; consider right knee MRI or orthopedics for persistent catching or true locking. Arrange modified work and review in 1 week. Fever, marked warmth, inability to bear weight or a locked knee warrants urgent reassessment.

2. If chronic symptoms persist, obtain weight-bearing radiographs when indicated and discuss strengthening/physical therapy and activity modification. Explain that degenerative changes may coexist with injury.

3. If crystal or septic arthritis remains possible with increasing warmth/effusion, arrange aspiration for crystals, cell count and culture before assuming gout. Review diuretic and gout management and safe anti-inflammatory options; explain that crystals do not exclude infection, with same-day evaluation for a hot swollen joint or fever.

walkthroughs.estimate_method: 150 spoken words/minute plus the full simulation examination durations and 55 seconds for introductions and transitions; explanatory commentary excluded. This is a planning estimate, not a measured student performance.

reasoning.question: Was swelling immediate or delayed, and is the knee truly locked?
reasoning.why: Use mechanism and mechanical symptoms while retaining crystal and infection safety checks.
reasoning.if_present: Use the reported pattern to select the relevant examinations and assess urgency.
reasoning.if_absent: Keep alternatives open and ask a focused follow-up.
reasoning.document: Separate reported symptoms, observed signs, assessment and proposed care.

differentials.name: Medial meniscal injury
differentials.teaching_context: Twisting mechanism, delayed effusion, medial joint-line tenderness and catching favor a meniscal injury.

differentials.name: Knee osteoarthritis with an acute flare
aliases: Knee osteoarthritis with an acute flare
differentials.teaching_context: Prior activity-related ache, brief stiffness and crepitus support underlying osteoarthritis.

differentials.name: Acute gouty arthritis
differentials.teaching_context: Prior crystal-proven gout, diuretic exposure and a warm effusion make crystal arthritis plausible, although this episode followed mechanical injury.

omissions: Explaining uncertainty and the practical follow-up plan.
